title: Added Value of HR-pQCT in Detecting Calcium Deposits in Rheumatoid Arthritis
official: Added Value of HR-pQCT: Detecting and Characterizing Calcium Deposits Suggestive of CPPD in the Hand and Wrist of Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients (HAND-QCT-RA)
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a high-resolution computed tomography scan (HR-pQCT) can detect and describe calcium crystal deposits in the hands and wrists of adults with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How often does the HR-pQCT scan detect calcium crystal deposits in the hand and wrist joints of people with RA?
* Can the HR-pQCT scan find calcium deposits that standard tests (x-rays and ultrasound) miss? Researchers will compare scan results from participants with RA to results from participants with known calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) and participants without joint inflammation.

During a single clinic visit, participants will:

* Have standard x-rays of their hands and wrists
* Have a routine ultrasound of their hands and wrists
* Have an HR-pQCT scan of their wrist and finger joints, which takes about 15 to 20 minutes and uses a very low dose of radiation

interventions.name: High-Resolution peripheral Quantitative Computed Tomography Imaging

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) Cohort:

* Age ≥ 60 years
* Diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis according to 2010 ACR/EULAR classification criteria
* Clinical diagnosis confirmed by an expert rheumatologist
* Current or past inflammatory involvement of the hand and/or wrist
* Written informed consent obtained

Calcium Pyrophosphate Deposition (CPPD) Cohort:

* Age ≥ 60 years
* Established diagnosis of CPPD based on synovial fluid crystal analysis and/or imaging findings compatible with current classification criteria
* Current or past inflammatory involvement of the hand and/or wrist
* Written informed consent obtained

Control Cohort (Non-inflammatory Controls):

* Age ≥ 60 years
* Outpatient evaluation at one of the participating centers for a condition not suggestive of CPPD, rheumatoid arthritis, erosive osteoarthritis, or other inflammatory joint diseases
* Clinical indication for conventional radiography of the hand and/or wrist as part of routine clinical practice
* Absence of past or present hand or wrist joint swelling suggestive of inflammatory arthritis
* Written informed consent obtained

Exclusion Criteria:

All Cohorts:

* Contraindications to CT-based imaging (including the inability to immobilize the hand and wrist during image acquisition)
* Known causes of secondary CPPD (e.g., hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatasia)
* Presence of hand/wrist prosthesis or osteosynthesis material interfering with image acquisition
* Inability to provide written informed consent
